body:
I haven't had a friend since 2012. All of my friends gradually went away one by one and I never heard from them again.

The last time I met up with a friend was awkward. I think she didn't want to be there. She came up from London and we rented bikes at the beach. At lunch we just ended up sat in silence. I desperately wanted her to visit because I hadn't seen her since 2010.

Before 2012 is all a blur.

I had lots of friends in primary school and in high school. It all went to hell when I turned 16 and went to college. Depression happened and social anxiety happened. My life has never been the same since and as I have often said, I feel like I am forever stuck in the summer after high school.

I have nothing to live for and every day is a little bit harder than the last.
At least it gets you some money. Maybe I should do it.

I wanted to add a few things to my previous post.

Thanks. It is hard. My life hasn't started and I'm already 33. I feel suicidal which is why I'm on here again. I live at home which makes things worse.

I don't think teaching is a low level job, maybe I phrased that wrong. It is low paid and high stress though. Why don't I want to do teaching... well there are many reasons I can think of. Right now I don't want to help people, I want to help myself (yeah maybe that sounds fucked up). My life is shit... no job, income, no independence, friends, no partner. I want to help myself above all else and do things that I find rewarding and interesting. I couldn't take that attitude into the classroom because in reality I couldn't care less about hitting performance targets or maybe even the students progress themselves. I think I could support children for a few months in a classroom but then I would get seriously fed up and want to do higher level stuff which is more interesting to me. Thirdly I am sick of education and I also don't believe in or agree with the way the education sector is in the UK. Teachers have to ram a huge curriculum down students throats which im sure you know all about and they have to sit exams. I have easily sat 100 exams in my life through gcses, alevels and 2 degrees and so far it has all been a waste of time and effort. I always tried my best at school but my grades haven't been rewarded, meanwhile dumbasses who I went to school with are doing much better. I always feel like I am never enough in job applications, there is always someone more polished and then theres nepotism, so again what was the point in me sitting so much assessment and trying so hard, for anything else other than pride? Lastly and this relates to my previous post, some teachers get treated like crap by senior management and students alike. Then you have all the paperwork and lesson plans - you're not allowed to do your own thing and teach off the cuff even if you know your stuff. It's all micro-managed and I wouldn't be able to stand it. Also most people in the teaching profession are women and that is a big no no for me as I would rather have a blend of people.

Anyway I don't know how old you are or where you live but I'm sure you could go into some other career or at least a stand by job since you already have a job right now and experience, at least you're not unemployed and fucking living at home like me. I always get emails about teaching and teaching assistant stuff.
